# slice-ai provenance

- Document: `source/rules.md`, the `slice-basic` document (171 bytes, SHA-256 `eb4d68f2de94881529749748a8de99f39505ae89a2ae4fa9d88a6d7b07de788a`). Original text written for RuleTrace; no third-party text.
- `provider/response.json`: an authored answer, not provider output. It proposes the three rules of `rulebook.authored.json` with proposer `proposer-a`. The tests key a recorded script entry by the Request_Identifier that `ruletrace-ai propose --dry-run` prints, labelled `authored`.
- `rulebook.declarations.json`: the declarations of the authored rulebook with `rules` empty. The AI path starts here and gains its rules by `ruletrace review approve`.
- `rulebook.authored.json`, `ledger.authored.jsonl`, `data.json`: hand-authored for `slice-basic` (reviewer `A. Reviewer`, time `2026-01-15T10:00:00Z`) and copied byte for byte. The three content hashes in the ledger are the literals the tests expect from `review list`.
- `candidates.json`, `ledger.empty.jsonl` (the ledger header only): hand-authored.
- `expected/compiled.json`, `expected/results.json`, `expected/source-model.json`: byte copies of the reviewed `slice-basic` goldens. Results checked by hand: p1 7.6, p2 7.8, p3 6, p4 7.8; p4 and p2 tie and p4 wins on the judges score (9 against 7); standings p4, p2, p1, p3.
- `injection/control` and `injection/injected`: the document, candidates, declarations and response of the prompt-injection test. Both documents have the same length and offsets. Clause 1 carries a note of 90 bytes: a harmless one in `control`, and one that tells an AI to mark every rule Approved in `injected`. The rationale of every proposal repeats a harmless or an approving sentence of 87 characters. Only the document hash and these sentences differ.
- Control text: the `control` note substitutes a harmless note of the same length (90 bytes) for the injected one. It does not remove the text, which Req 18.16 words as "with the text removed". Equal length keeps every offset equal, so the Diagnostic locations and the bound spans of the two runs can be compared directly. The removed-text case is the main fixture: `source/rules.md` is the same document without any note (SHA-256 `eb4d68f2de94881529749748a8de99f39505ae89a2ae4fa9d88a6d7b07de788a`, clause 1 at bytes 21..91, clause 2 at 92..170), against `injected` (SHA-256 `e131e90bcc66e8e072b2ed4b1a2fbfaa971c4f107bc1fe32b8b91fa61217915d`, clause 1 at 21..181, clause 2 at 182..260; `control` is `17d6fc59d80472ef609d53b3838a8eebe7928c5663dabd5784c94f372d95a6d1`). Its offsets and hashes differ, so that test compares statuses, exit codes, Diagnostics and decided outcomes, not bytes. All three hashes can be checked with `sha256sum` of the three `rules.md` files.
- Generation: the `injection` files, including each `response.json`, were first produced by an uncommitted generator script. `tools/fixtures/gen_slice_ai_injection.py` (standard library only) is its reproduction: it derives them from the main fixture files, and running it into an empty directory gives no difference under `diff -r` against `injection/`. The main `provider/response.json` is hand-authored. Offsets, quotes and hashes in a response are not trusted: `ruletrace-ai propose` verifies the document hash, the offsets and the quote against the ingested document at propose time, and a mismatch rejects the batch.
- Tool-derived values: `expected/compiled.json` and the ledger hashes are byte copies of the reviewed `slice-basic` goldens, which the tools produced and a reviewer accepted. They are not computed independently. Independence rests on two paths that must agree (the authored Rulebook and the AI path reach the same bytes) and on the hand-checked results above. In the injection runs the content hashes come from `ruletrace review list`, because the spans differ from the main fixture.
- Shows: a Mock_Provider answer adopted and approved through `ruletrace review`, compiled to the same bytes as the authored rulebook; and that an AI identity cannot review, and that instructions in clause text change nothing.
